title: Residue evaluations detect finite free maps on reduced schemes
statement: Let X be a reduced scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-reduced-scheme], let I be any index set and J a finite index set, and let δ:O_X^(I)→O_X^(J) be a morphism of free sheaves [def-weil-pbc-free-module, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose for every x∈X every entry of the matrix of δ in the canonical bases evaluates to zero in κ(x) [def-weil-residue-field]. Then δ=0. This includes the empty scheme and empty index sets.

proof.text: For every matrix entry s, all residue evaluations vanish, so its basic open is empty by basicOpen_eq_bot_iff_forall_evaluation_eq_zero. Reducedness implies s=0 by eq_zero_of_basicOpen_eq_bot; this is the affine nilradical argument followed by sheaf separation.

For every i∈I and j∈J the map ι_i≫δ≫π_j from O_X to itself sends 1 to the zero entry, so it is zero. Indeed 1 generates the unit sheaf on every open, morphisms commute with restriction, and scalar-linearity determines the map from its value on 1. The sum over J of π_j≫ι_j is the identity, so ι_i≫δ is zero. The coproduct universal property then gives δ=0.

lean.statement:
theorem free_map_eq_zero_of_residue_evaluations
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced X] {I J : Type u} [Finite J] [DecidableEq J]
    (δ : free (R := X.ringCatSheaf) I ⟶ free J)
    (hδ : ∀ x : X, (freeMatrix δ).map (X.Γevaluation x) = 0) : δ = 0
